title: Check: a mapped share that answers only after 'Drives' is shown gets its button in letter order (Windows Sandbox, silenced loopback share woken at about 20 s and about 120 s)
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: 1. A share that answers only after 'Drives' is shown, woken at about 20 s, gets its button in the real app: missing
2. The same share woken at about 120 s gets its button in the real app: missing
3. The late button sits between its letter neighbours in the real app: missing
4. A way to read the drive buttons (letters, order) and DriveStatus unattended in the Sandbox, after the late arrival: missing

No engine-runnable command reproduces the silenced-share arms. They need LanmanServer stopped and an SMB mapping, so they ran through the Sandbox tool, about 10 runs of the runner (the last of which reproduced the 20 s arm and the negative control). The named host test feeds their recorded results into the verdict.

No product change. Q-007's 'no, not always' (a woken share whose blocked read fails at the wake gets no button until relaunch) is recorded as a finding, not fixed: the design builds the check, and the fix would be a new behaviour that needs a decision.
A no-path launch's DriveStatus is still unreadable (Q-009's other half). The drives mode holds a report, and a no-path launch has none.

PRODUCT FINDING (answers Q-007/U-007): in 2 of 9 Sandbox arms woken at about 120 s, the share's blocked IsReady call ended at the wake without finishing. Its read thread went away and no button was ever added, because ReadDrive returns null on not-ready or IOException and nothing re-reads. The 20 s arm held 9 of 9. U-007's expected '~60 s client give-up' did not happen: the SMB client opened a second connection at about +70 s and kept waiting, and the failures came only at the wake. Decide whether to re-read a drive that answers not-ready after the picker settled. That would be a workaround for an outside SMB-client defect, so the standing rule applies: its own checkbox in Settings, on by default, a notice in the app, and an entry in the workaround list.

Update Q-007 and U-007 in the ledger with the measured split (20 s: 9/9; 120 s: 7/9). The runner's `-Wake 20,20,120,120,120` repeats arms; the failing runs' inputs are rows R5 and R6 of tests/window/SL-004-LateShareCorpus.json.

StartupHook.cs changed, which is on the network-pass staleness list (docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:239-249). By the project's own rule the person's network check (N-001 to N-004 plus StalledShareTests) is stale. The design assigned that to SC-006.

The full suite shows timing flakes under load: UnfinishedTests.StopsInTheSizeChecksMarkWhatAPendingCheckCouldChange (workers: 4), the baseline flake from the build-check, and once DefenderStateRecordTests (a Controlled Folder Access read timed out at 20 s). Both pass alone. A first red run had 3 failures I did not capture by name.

deviation: DrivePanel.buttons reads 3 in a passing run (C:, Y:, Z:), not the design's 2. A SUBST Z: neighbour with a later letter is added, because without one appending at the end and inserting in letter order give the same result (build-check). The check asserts Y: sits between C: and Z: and that the report's count equals the buttons the hook logged.

deviation: The design gave no instrument for reading the buttons unattended. I added the `drives` hook mode (build-check criterion 4, U-007, Q-009 named it). It needs a root and --report, so a no-path launch is still unreadable.

deviation: 'Records whether the read returned not-ready or was still blocked' is done from outside the app. The runner reads each thread's OS name (GetThreadDescription) for 'FsAnalyser drive read N'. It could not be done in the hook, because the fitness rule InteropLivesOnlyInNative bars Library/DllImport from tests/**/*.cs outside an allow-list. .NET thread names do reach the OS: verified in the Sandbox, where the share's read thread showed alive for the whole silence.

deviation: The Sandbox runner uses `net use` to map the loopback share, which the fitness rule 'only the shared rig changes SMB client mappings (PowerShell)' forbids in tests/**/*.ps1. I added one except_files entry for that script. It refuses to run unless C:\Users\WDAGUtilityAccount exists, so it cannot stop a person's file server (verified: refuses on this PC, runs in the Sandbox).
deviation: The Sandbox bootstrap passed to the Sandbox tool is a one-line call to the in-tree runner, so the engine's task.ps1 never names the exe, which keeps AppArgumentTests green (lesson #889).
